rationale: Cache-line optimization is critical for MACH-1000 performance. 16-byte Variant packs 4 per 64-byte cache line vs ~2.6 for 24-byte. Decimal fits exactly in 14-byte payload + 2-byte tag. COM ABI bridging handled at boundary, not in hot-path layout.
NaN-boxing analysis is sound — 51 usable bits cannot represent Decimal's 96-bit integer + scale. Include analysis as explicit design rationale to prevent future re-investigation.
SSO for strings <=14 bytes eliminates heap allocation for the majority of VBA string temporaries (cell references, short labels, error codes). Major win for string-heavy VBA code.

Finger trees are theoretically elegant but exotic in Rust (no mature crate). Adapt: document finger-tree-inspired design goal but implement with tiered SmallVec/ThinVec initially, with finger-tree upgrade path when incremental reparsing demands it.
Combinator-based rewriting over immutable trees is natural for the Red/Green architecture. Enables parallel speculative optimization passes. Integrate as the transform model for the IR pipeline.

MLIR concept is exactly right — progressive lowering preserves domain semantics for VBA-aware optimization. But we won't use actual MLIR (C++ dependency violates values #4/#5). Implement as Rust-native multi-level IR with three tiers: VbaHir → VbaMir → CfgIr. This becomes a new crate: oxvba-ir.

Brilliant insight. On Error Resume Next creates irreducible CFGs if naively lowered. Modeling it as a guarded region in VbaHir and delaying expansion to CfgIr preserves optimization opportunities in earlier passes. Direct accept.

SWAR broadword decoding is a proven Knuth technique. O(1) per 64-bit block for opcode pattern scanning eliminates branch misprediction in the interpreter hot path. Accept for the VM interpreter fast path.

The MMIX register-window insight is the single most impactful change. Pure stack VMs have inherently high memory traffic. However: fully replacing stack-based design is a major commitment. Adapt: design a hybrid register-window VM as the primary execution engine, with the register-window approach for the interpreter. The bytecode format becomes register-based, not stack-based. Cranelift translation also benefits (register IR → register IR).

Boundary-tag allocation is well-understood and directly applicable to BStr/SafeArray pools. O(1) coalescing addresses fragmentation in long-running Excel automation workloads. Accept as the allocation strategy for the VBA-specific heap.
rkyv zero-copy deserialization via mmap eliminates startup allocation for large macro corpora. Aligns with performance value. Accept for the bytecode serialization format.

Verus is promising but immature for a project of this scope. The Lean 4 formalization already covers coercion correctness. Defer Verus integration until the Lean specifications are stable and we have concrete unsafe code that would benefit.
Creusot has the same maturity concern as Verus. Semantic preservation proofs for IR lowering are valuable but premature — we need to build the IR first. Defer to post-Phase 3.

Kani is the most immediately actionable formal verification tool for Rust unsafe code. Bounded model checking for broadword masks, union loads, and register window bounds is concrete and achievable. Add to CI pipeline alongside Miri.

The enhanced Red/Green description with relative-width-only green nodes and ephemeral red wrappers is already implicit in the baseline plan but deserves explicit, detailed treatment. Accept and expand.
This is the motivation for MK001. Accept as explicit architectural rationale — the 24-byte layout is identified as a performance ceiling and the 16-byte layout is the resolution.

Cycle detection latency spikes are real but the Bacon-Rajan collector is already opt-in in the baseline plan. Adapt: add explicit documentation that the cycle detector is scheduled (not concurrent), with configurable trigger thresholds. Epoch-based batching to amortize cost.
This is the motivation for MK006. The semantic gap between AST and stack-VM/Cranelift is real. The multi-level IR resolves it. Accept as architectural rationale.
